---
title: "Expected and state-specific reporting loss"
subtitle: "3.11 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 16–18 and vignette m2"
description: "Comparison of minimum expected loss with realised losses in paired posterior draws."
---

A report that minimises posterior expected loss need not have the smallest loss in every latent state. The display
holds an optimal report and a comparator fixed, then evaluates both on the same complete posterior draws. The
probability that the comparator has smaller realised loss and the mean magnitude of the loss difference describe
different properties. The finite-state example provides exact probabilities; the simulations additionally show
Monte Carlo variation. The optimality comparison requires a common law and loss, and membership of the comparator
in the optimised family.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Inside the family.** Among 63 reports with at most two grades, the best has conditional risk .0940; the two
  posterior-mean tiers have .1046. Yet that common rule wins 57 of these 100 paired draws. Loss magnitudes matter,
  not just how often a report wins. Below the dashed diagonal the common rule has smaller realised loss.
- **Outside the family.** The comparison retains the two-grade family but uses a three-tier comparator. Its conditional
  risk .0417 is below .0940. It was excluded from the family optimised here, so the earlier guarantee does not
  cover it. The law and the optimised family have stayed fixed.
- **Two-state law.** The best report withholds at risk .2500; the expected-rank order has risk .3000. Nevertheless
  the rule wins with exact probability .700 and wins 65 of these 100 sampled draws. The state table gives exact
  probabilities and losses; the scatter remains a sample.
- **A short run.** The rule wins 9 of 10 draws, and the paired mean difference is −.00667, favoring it in this
  finite sample. The exact conditional difference is positive; the paired Monte Carlo SE quantifies numerical sampling variation.
- **A silent common rule.** Its risk is .2000 and its disclosed-error fraction is “NA: no disclosure.” Silence
  costs τ per pair, so a report that states nothing does not have zero reporting loss.
- **Identical reports.** The summary reads “ties 100”: both reports have the same loss in every drawn state.
  Draw selection gives the corresponding state, grades and wrong counts.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Total reporting loss includes wrong stated directions and the withholding cost, divided by all pairs. A wrong
fraction divides by stated pairs instead. Conditional dominance requires the same law, loss and optimisation
family, including comparator membership; it does not establish superiority at every state or under fixed-truth
remeasurement. The paired SE measures sampling of the difference, not uncertainty about the supplied model.
:::
